result.note: Tests the March 2026 defence approvals: service-wise allocation of platforms, the separate Tunguska contract with Russia, and the record FY 2025-26 approval and contract totals.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, India approved USD 25 billion in military purchases. Consider the following pairs of items and the service they were approved for:
items: S-400 missile systems — Indian Air Force
questions.ask: How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.explain: Only the S-400 pair is correct. Dhanush guns went to the Army, and Su-30 engine overhauls went to the Air Force. The package was India's second major defence approval in as many months.
questions.source: The Air Force gets S-400s, medium transport aircraft, unmanned attack drones, and Su-30 engine overhauls.

questions.prompt: In March 2026, alongside a USD 25 billion package of defence approvals, India signed a separate USD 47 million contract with Russia. Which system did this contract cover?
questions.explain: The separate USD 47 million contract with Moscow covers Tunguska air defence systems. It was signed alongside approvals that also included Russian S-400 missile systems for the Air Force.
questions.source: A separate USD 47 million contract was also signed with Moscow, covering Tunguska air defence systems.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about India's defence procurement in the fiscal year 2025-26, as reported in March 2026:
items: India approved 55 proposals worth 6.73 trillion rupees (USD 71 billion), a historic high.
India signed contracts for 503 proposals amounting to 6.73 trillion rupees.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong. The contracts signed for 503 proposals amounted to 2.28 trillion rupees, while 6.73 trillion rupees was the value of the 55 approved proposals. The spending follows the four-day clash with Pakistan in 2025, which exposed gaps in drone saturation, battlefield communications and rapid deployment.
questions.source: In all, India has approved 55 proposals worth 6.73 trillion rupees (USD 71 billion) and signed contracts for another 503 proposals amounting to 2.28 trillion rupees in this fiscal year, marking a historic high.
